title: Southrepps X.3023 Memorial
crew_summary: 3 killed (1 survived); including Sgt. Jack Leonard Frederick Ottaway
narrative: In the early hours of 20 November 1940, Hampden X3023 of 44 Squadron took off from RAF Waddington in Lincolnshire for a long-range bombing mission against an oil refinery at Lutzkendorf near Leipzig in central Germany. The Hampden was one of Bomber Command's principal medium bombers in the early war years, a narrow-fuselage aircraft that earned the nickname "the flying suitcase" for its cramped crew positions. On the return flight, navigational difficulties -- compounded by darkness and poor weather -- led the aircraft far off course over Norfolk. At approximately 06:20 hours, the Hampden crashed into woodland in the grounds of Templewood House at Northrepps, a shooting lodge near the Norfolk coast. Three of the four crew members -- pilot Sergeant Jack Ottaway, navigator Pilot Officer Archie Kerr, and wireless operator/air gunner Sergeant Stanley Elliott -- were killed on impact. The fourth crew member, Sergeant Stanley Hird, an air gunner, survived the crash and went on to serve with the RAF for the remainder of the war. The crash site remained relatively unknown for decades until local historians began researching the incident. The proximity of the crash to the radar station at nearby Bard Hill -- which would later claim another bomber crew in 1945 -- is a poignant reminder of the dangers that Norfolk's coastal landscape posed to returning aircraft.

crew.name: Stanley Hird
crew.burial_location: Survived; continued RAF service until war's end

cause_of_loss: Navigational error on return; aircraft struck trees in poor visibility
operation_target: Bombing sortie to oil refinery at Lutzkendorf, near Leipzig
